chronicle.text: Gaiheim took food that Zosik had left, and was seen: the first theft from a store.
Zosik found that what Zeitouzi had told them was wrong, and trusted them less for it.
Miyedil tied fiber and fiber together with fiber and was left with something to carry things in: the first carrier.
Youmerei gathered food that had grown where seeds had been dropped: the first harvest from seed left in the ground.
Tamin tied wood and wood together with fiber and was left with something that floats and carries someone across water: the first raft.
Tamin tied stone and wood together with fiber and was left with something heavy on a handle: the first club.
Saigel scratched a mark <^\/> into the ground.
Zosik went back to a thing they had made a third time, to see it happen again: the first deliberate testing.
Zosik attacked Gaiheim: the first violence.
Disos told Shogal that Yumougu could be believed: reputation passed on by word.
Touhas struck flint with flint and stared at what happened.
Touhas struck flint with flint and was left with a sharp edge: the first blade.
Touhas came back for food left 10 weeks before, and it was still there.
Zosik crossed open water on something that floats and came ashore on land nobody could walk to from where they set out.
Youmerei crossed open water on something that floats and came ashore on land nobody could walk to from where they set out.
Hadai drank from the sea and it did not quench their thirst.
Zosik buried seed on purpose, having seen it come back as food: the beginning of farming.
Keman took in the orphan Shivain, no relation, the first time a stranger raised another's child.
Zosik killed Miyedil after being attacked by Miyedil in year 3.
Revenge answered revenge: the feud between the kin of Zosik and the kin of Miyedil had begun.
Gaiheim killed Zosik after being attacked by Zosik in year 2.
Shivain struck flint where dry things lay, and they caught: the first fire made by people.
Shivain tied a blade and a wood flake together with fiber and was left with a sharp point on a long shaft: the first spear.
Saigel crossed open water on something that floats and came ashore on land nobody could walk to from where they set out.
Thokithoun tied a club and a carrier together with fiber and was left with something warm to wear: the first wrap.
3 people now take the mark <|ov> to go with flint being struck, and have for two years. Nobody decided this; it grew from where the mark was made and seen.
Viyikik took up striking stone with stone from a mark: the first thing learned from a record.
Viyikik came on the mark <\./> and took it to mean stone being struck: the first mark read as a message.
Viyikik found that what the mark <\./> seemed to say was wrong, and put less faith in that mark.
At (28, 9) the heap of things people had left grew big enough to keep out a fifth of the winter cold: the first dwelling. Keman had put in the most.
3 people now tell that Yumougu attacked Bebovein. It was Shogal. The story changed as it was passed on.
3 people now take the mark <v-\> to go with flint being struck, and have for two years. Nobody decided this; it grew from where the mark was made and seen.
3 people now take the mark <v-|> to go with a grave, and have for two years. Nobody decided this; it grew from where the mark was made and seen.
Hadai set food aside on purpose, having found it there when it was needed before: the beginning of keeping stores.
3 people now take the mark <-/\> to go with seed sown in summer, and have for two years. Nobody decided this; it grew from where the mark was made and seen.
7 people now take the mark <.-v> to go with a grave, and have for two years. Nobody decided this; it grew from where the mark was made and seen.

3 people now tell that Varok attacked Shogal. It was Bebovein. The story changed as it was passed on.
The mark <-/\> has drifted: it went with seed sown in summer, and now, for 4 people, with seed sown in winter.
The mark <v-|> has drifted: it went with a grave, and now, for 3 people, with stone being struck.
15 people now take the mark <v-o> to go with seed sown in spring, and have for two years. Nobody decided this; it grew from where the mark was made and seen.
